class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, width=256, blocks=3):
        super().__init__()
        self.joint_emb = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(17, width) * 0.02)
        self.in_joint = nn.Linear(3 + 2 + 1, width)
        self.global_in = nn.Linear(3 + 64, width)
        layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model=width, nhead=4, dim_feedforward=width * 2, batch_first=True, activation="gelu", norm_first=True)
        self.blocks = nn.TransformerEncoder(layer, num_layers=blocks)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(width)
        self.out = nn.Linear(width, 3)

    def forward(self, x, t, c):
        xj = x.reshape(-1, 17, 3)
        kp = c[:, :34].reshape(-1, 17, 2)
        mk = c[:, 34:51].reshape(-1, 17, 1)
        fr = c[:, 51:54]
        h = self.in_joint(torch.cat([xj, kp, mk], dim=-1)) + self.joint_emb[None, :, :]
        h = h + self.global_in(torch.cat([fr, sinusoidal(t)], dim=1))[:, None, :]
        return self.out(self.norm(self.blocks(h))).reshape(-1, 51)

candidates.rationale: FiLM modulation re-injects the 2D condition and flow time into every block, preventing conditioning from being washed out by the residual MLP.
SwiGLU gated residual blocks give the velocity field more expressive per-layer nonlinearity at the same width without changing the overall topology.
A skeleton-graph token network propagates information only along anatomical joint connections, providing a local structural prior complementary to flat MLPs.

    def __init__(self, width):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.LayerNorm(width), nn.Linear(width, width), nn.GELU(), nn.Linear(width, width)
        )
        self.film = nn.Linear(width, 2 * width)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.film.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.film.bias)

    def forward(self, h, cond):
        scale, shift = self.film(cond).chunk(2, dim=-1)
        return h + self.net(h * (1.0 + scale) + shift)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, width=512, blocks=3):
        super().__init__()
        self.inp = nn.Linear(51, width)
        self.cond = nn.Linear(54 + 64, width)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([Block(width) for _ in range(blocks)])
        self.out = nn.Linear(width, 51)

    def forward(self, x, t, c):
        cond = self.cond(torch.cat([c, sinusoidal(t)], dim=1))
        h = self.inp(x) + cond
        for block in self.blocks:
            h = block(h, cond)
        return self.out(h)</replace>

class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, width=192, blocks=4):
        super().__init__()
        edges = [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 3), (2, 4), (5, 6), (5, 7), (7, 9), (6, 8), (8, 10), (5, 11), (6, 12), (11, 12), (11, 13), (13, 15), (12, 14), (14, 16), (0, 5), (0, 6)]
        adj = torch.eye(17)
        for i, j in edges:
            adj[i, j] = 1.0
            adj[j, i] = 1.0
        self.register_buffer("adj", adj / adj.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True))
        self.joint_emb = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(17, width) * 0.02)
        self.in_joint = nn.Linear(3 + 2 + 1, width)
        self.global_in = nn.Linear(3 + 64, width)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([Block(width) for _ in range(blocks)])
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(width)
        self.out = nn.Linear(width, 3)

    def forward(self, x, t, c):
        xj = x.reshape(-1, 17, 3)
        kp = c[:, :34].reshape(-1, 17, 2)
        mk = c[:, 34:51].reshape(-1, 17, 1)
        fr = c[:, 51:54]
        h = self.in_joint(torch.cat([xj, kp, mk], dim=-1)) + self.joint_emb[None, :, :]
        h = h + self.global_in(torch.cat([fr, sinusoidal(t)], dim=1))[:, None, :]
        for block in self.blocks:
            h = block(torch.einsum("ij,bjd->bid", self.adj, h))
        return self.out(self.norm(h)).reshape(-1, 51)</replace>
